mechanism_narrative: The sharp same-week collapse in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES will suppress discretionary trips to malls, restaurants, and shops over the next four weeks, pushing RETAIL_REC below its prior four-week average.
evidence_refs: fact:week t-0w shows TRANSIT at -35.6 and WORKPLACES at -26.4
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean within 28 days after a comparable simultaneous drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM rises above about 10 points while RETAIL_REC is already deeply negative, households are substituting essential trips for discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC should remain lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:week t-0w shows GROCERY_PHARM at 10.7 and RETAIL_REC at -39.1
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rebounds within 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying above +10, the substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A joint decline in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates people are avoiding outdoor and neighborhood activity altogether; that broad pullback should keep retail visitation depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:week t-0w shows PARKS at -16.3 and RESIDENTIAL at 10.4 after earlier PARKS strength faded
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while PARKS is falling and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, the broad-avoidance mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The steep reversal from positive PARKS mobility to negative PARKS mobility marks a weather- or event-related demand shock that usually spills into lower discretionary retail activity within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0 after being positive in the prior two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from 26.9 at t-3w to -16.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not weaken in the week after PARKS crosses from positive to negative, the seasonal spillover is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Once TRANSIT drops more than 20 points week-on-week, commuting frictions intensify and retail trips are postponed, so RETAIL_REC should be lower over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 20 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -0.4 at t-1w to -35.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline after a >20-point weekly TRANSIT drop, the transit-friction mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in WORKPLACES above zero while TRANSIT stays near or below zero should raise daytime foot traffic and nearby discretionary spending, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES turns positive while TRANSIT is at or below 0
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES was still positive at t-2w and t-3w before dropping to -26.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls when WORKPLACES recovers above zero despite weak TRANSIT, the commuting spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Very high GROCERY_PHARM combined with very low RETAIL_REC signals household stockpiling and precautionary shopping; this state predicts further retail weakness over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w shows GROCERY_PHARM at 10.7 while RETAIL_REC is -39.1
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rebounds materially despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining elevated, the stockpiling mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, simultaneous declines in TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and PARKS indicate broad mobility suppression that should keep retail-and-recreation mobility below its recent average throughout the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w shows TRANSIT -35.6, WORKPLACES -26.4, and PARKS -16.3
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while all three proxies remain depressed, the broad-suppression mechanism is rejected.
